transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-12-30 10:00am PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Thompson (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Sarah Kim (CISO, Glenvale), Raj Patel (Lead Engineer), Lena Ortiz (Compliance)

Summary:
Quick sync on security items for the POC: SSO/SAML setup, audit logs collection and retention, SOC2 artifacts, KMS/encryption and RBAC, plus a short discussion on data residency and production rollout gating. Agreed next steps and owners.

Topics:
- SSO SAML mapping / test account
- Audit logs schema and forwarding (SIEM integration)
- Data retention policy during pilot vs production
- SOC2 / pen test artifacts and timelines
- KMS / encryption at rest and in transit, HSM question

Action items (captured above)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um quick check-in for the weekly security sync for the Glenvale POC. Sarah, Lena, Raj, good to see you. Diego and I from Redwood.
[00:12] Sarah: Hi, thanks Maya. We're short on time this morning, so if we can focus SSO and audit logs that would be great.
[00:20] Maya: Yep totally. Diego will lead the technical bits. Diego, do you want to start with SAML?
[00:25] Diego: Sure. So current state, we have a staging tenant spun up for Glenvale, and I configured a basic SP with the metadata you gave last week. We need the SAML metadata from your side for the IdP in staging or a test account to validate attribute mapping (email, uid, roles).
[00:42] Raj: Yeah, we hit an issue last run where role mapping wasn't passed through – the claims were named differently in our IdP. I can export the metadata but I also need to confirm the attribute names.
[00:52] Diego: Right, we can do an attribute mapping step, we can also map on Redwood side. One note — the SE console will show user and session ids in the audit logs, but if you want role names, we need the attribute present in the SAML assertion or we'll map via LDAP lookup.
[01:08] Lena: From compliance perspective we need roles preserved and an audit trail showing role changes. Also retention for logs needs to be at least 90 days for some lines of business, but pilot we discussed a shorter retention to limit exposure.
[01:22] Maya: Ok so two retention windows: pilot default 30 days, but we can propose an optional 90-day long-tail archived store. We'll put that in the next steps.
[01:30] Sarah: About audit logs — can you confirm the log schema and delivery options? We need to push to our SIEM (Splunk) and also have S3 bucket export for longer-term retention.
[01:40] Diego: Yes, Redwood can stream audit logs via Kinesis or direct S3 exports, and we also support syslog or webhooks, although syslog may need a collector. The schema includes timestamp, actor, action, resource, request id, session id, model id, token usage. I should warn the auto transcript generator sometimes calls model id 'mod-id' in the logs, so don't trust example names in the UI, ha.
[02:02] Raj: For ingestion to our Splunk, we prefer S3 + Lambda -> Kinesis forwarder. Is there cost impact for higher audit volume?
[02:10] Diego: There's small cost for audit storage and egress if you pull logs; during the POC we can use our staging bucket with minimal retention to reduce costs. For production we'd negotiate retention + export cadence.
[02:22] Sarah: Encryption: are logs encrypted at rest? We need KMS-managed keys, ideally customer-managed keys (CMK).
[02:30] Diego: Yes, logs at rest are encrypted. For Private deployments we absolutely do CMK / HSM. For hosted POC we offer customer-managed KMS in your account (or we can use ours with a rotation note). We also encrypt in transit with TLS.
[02:42] Lena: For SOC2 evidence, we need the configuration and key management doc and proof of key rotation.
[02:48] Maya: We'll include SOC2 Type II report and the pen-test summary in the packet. I'll share those docs by Jan 3.
[02:56] Sarah: Great. On SSO: we need SAML metadata and a staging test user. Raj can provide metadata but also need Redwood to create a test SP endpoint in staging.
[03:06] Raj: I'll get the metadata today or tomorrow. Also one question on SCIM — do you support automatic user provisioning?
[03:12] Diego: Yes we support SCIM for provisioning, currently in our hosted offering it's supported as beta. For the pilot we can do manual provisioning or SCIM if you want to enable it; SCIM will sync groups/roles which solves the attribute mapping problem.
[03:24] Sarah: SCIM would be nice but it might take extra approvals from our identity team. For now let's do SAML mapping plus one manual test user.
[03:32] Diego: Sounds good. Next, a couple minutes on data residency: you mentioned in the RFI that some data must stay in us-east-1. We're currently hosting the pilot in us-east-1 — are you ok with that?
[03:44] Raj: Yes US-east for pilot is fine. For production we'll need explicit region tenancy and contract language.
[03:50] Maya: We'll note region tenancy as a gating item for production.
[03:54] Lena: SOC2 and data residency plus the audit log retention are the big gating items from compliance. Also we want to confirm background pen test status — do you have a timeline?
[04:04] Maya: We completed a pen test Q3; I'll include the summary and high-level remediation items. For production we'll coordinate a customer-facing assessment if needed.
[04:12] Diego: One more technical item — KMS sign-in for model artifacts, do you plan to upload any customer PII into prompts?
[04:20] Sarah: We won't send raw PII in probe prompts, but eventual production flows will include customer-identifiable metadata. Need to ensure redaction or tokenization.
[04:28] Diego: We have built-in PII redaction knobs and you can also configure request-side transformers to strip PII before it hits the model. We'll demo the audit logs that show redaction events.
[04:38] Raj: How does Redwood handle KV cache and prefix caching vis-a-vis audit logs? We saw a note about cache hits in the dashboard.
[04:46] Diego: The cache is at inference runtime and does not store user tokens persistently; audit logs will record cache hits as metric entries but not dump the content of the KV. I will double-check the exact fields.
[04:56] Lena: Also need RBAC for console access — we require two-person approvals for any key rotation events in prod. Is RBAC granular?
[05:04] Diego: We support org-level RBAC and per-route roles; we can integrate with your SAML groups for role mapping. Approvals are currently tracked via audit logs; for two-person approval we can add an approval workflow as a service or integrate with your ticketing system.
[05:18] Sarah: Ok good. Last item — SLA for uptime/incident response in dedicated vs hosted? We have questions on mean time to respond and on-call.
[05:28] Maya: For Dedicated we offer SLA-backed uptime and faster incident response; for hosted POC you'll be on standard support but we'll assign a CSM and SE for the pilot. We can include a contact list in the follow-up.
[05:39] Raj: Cool. Any blockers for the pilot continuing?
[05:43] Lena: Only outstanding is SAML metadata and confirmation of 90-day retention for these specific LOBs; otherwise we're fine to proceed.
[05:50] Maya: Great. To recap — Maya will send SOC2 + pen test + infra diagram by Jan 3; Diego will stand up SSO staging SP and run audit log demo and record; Raj will send SAML metadata and staging test creds by Jan 5; Lena will confirm retention preference. We'll reconvene next week same time.
[06:08] Sarah: Thanks everyone.
[06:10] Maya: Thanks, bye.
